[artless] If you prefer the spray version, 473ml can be bought for $26.99 ($16.99 with email voucher) at BCF.
[starbearer] is there something like this which prevents the insides of a car from fogging up?
I do use the defogger but don't like the hot air blowing around in the car too much
[Golazo] https://www.rainx.com.au/interior-glass-anti-fog/
Of the 88 reviews on Super Cheap website, 27 are 1-star.
https://www.supercheapauto.com.au/p/rain-x-rain-x-interior-g…
[OZKap] Anti-fog.
We've used Rain-X brand as well as bar's bugs anti-fog. Both seem to work pretty well.
[starbearer] you mean this one: https://www.repco.com.au/car-care-panel/car-care/windscreen-…
[Nom] prevents the insides of a car from fogging up
@starbearer Step 1, press the AUTO button on your climate control and then leave it alone.
The end.
If you leave the climate set to auto, it'll run the air conditioner, keep the temperature at the comfortable level you've chosen, and your windows won't steam up.
[starbearer] Older car mate. No auto climate control. I need to select the temps.
[Nom] Then make sure you leave the AC on and the recirculation mode off. The AC will remove some moisture from the incoming air.
[starbearer] @Nom: yea I do that currently. but wondering if the anti-fog products are worth it
[Nom] @starbearer: If you run the AC and have at least a little airflow heading towards the glass, then you shouldn't steam up.
Have you checked all the carpet etc is completely dry ? It sounds like you might have a slight water leak - the AC should be more than capable of drying the interior.
[Brick50] Anyone else find rain X causes your windscreen to be covered in little droplets which actually make it harder to see at low speeds? I find it’s not worth the down side
